family: One fixed total family f_N on {0,1}^N, defined for every integer N>=1 by proof.md Section 1. Set k(m) = the least prime > 2*m^(3/5) and N(m) = m + k(m); let m(N) be the largest m with N(m) <= N. Read the input as a prefix q in {0,1}^k with k = k(m(N)), a payload y in {0,1}^m with m = m(N), and an ignored tail. Let Q(Z) = Z^k + sum_{i<k} q_i Z^i. If Q is not irreducible over F_2 the value is 0; otherwise, in F = F_2[Z]/(Q) with polynomial basis 1..Z^(k-1), split the payload into r = ceil(m/k) k-bit blocks (zero-padded last block) giving phi_i(y) in F, put y_i = phi_i(y)^(2^(i+1)-1), let Sym_r^t be the t-th elementary symmetric polynomial with t = ceil(sqrt(r)), and output the constant coefficient of Sym_r^t(y_1,...,y_r). The same deterministic polynomial-time algorithm (prime scan, Rabin irreducibility test, field arithmetic, division-free symmetric-polynomial recurrence) computes every f_N; the language is in P, hence in NP with empty witnesses.
theorem: For this one fixed total uniform family, at actual input length N and in the full Li-Yang B2 model, C_B2(f_N) >= (7/2)*N - 67*N^(4/5) for every integer N >= 2^10; hence liminf over N of C_B2(f_N)/N >= 7/2, so the declared finite projection (7/2, 1) holds. Proof: fix a valid prefix and the zero tail, restricting to an m(N)-dimensional affine slice on which f_N is the Ben-Sasson-Kopparty affine disperser of dimension floor(6*m^(4/5))+1; the slice circuit computes that disperser, so the gate elimination theorem for affine dispersers (framework.md, Theorem A: every B2 circuit for an affine disperser of dimension d has at least 3.5n-7d gates) gives C_B2(f_N) >= (7/2)*m(N) - 42*m(N)^(4/5) - 7, and m(N) >= N - 7*N^(3/5) - 1 yields the stated remainder. Both directions of NP membership, all integer lengths and an explicit N_epsilon = max(2^10, ceil((67/epsilon)^5)) are established in proof.md.
